narrative.coaching_note: The one change to make next time is to wash your hands with soap and water after touching the area around the bed and before touching resident A. You touched bed rail A at 1.6 seconds, and that contamination moved with your bare hand to call button at 7.6 seconds and to phone at 12.4 seconds. You then touched resident A at 21.4 seconds without cleaning your hands, which missed the moment after touching the surroundings at 11 seconds and the moment before touching the resident at 21.4 seconds. Because this was C. difficile, alcohol rub does not kill the spores, so use soap and water for the full 40 seconds. Washing at that point would have kept bare hand, gloved hand, phone, and resident A clean.
narrative.audit_summary: Staged clip with C. difficile source bed rail A. Bare hand touched bed rail A at 1.6 seconds, with onward transfer to bare hand at 1.6 seconds, to call button at 7.6 seconds, to phone at 12.4 seconds, and to resident A at 21.4 seconds, producing one exposure of resident A. Hand hygiene compliance was 0/2 opportunities: Moment 1 0/1 missed at 21.4 seconds, Moment 5 0/1 missed at 11 seconds. No hygiene events occurred; alcohol rub does not kill C. difficile spores, soap and water is required. No glove use issues were noted. Contamination remained on bare hand, gloved hand, bed rail A, call button, phone, and resident A. Surfaces flagged were bed rail A, call button, phone, and resident A; use an EPA List K sporicidal disinfectant (effective against C. difficile spores).
narrative.top_fix: The highest-impact single change in this clip was hand hygiene with soap and water at 11 seconds.
